In clinical trials, data is abundant and critical. Understanding, 
interpreting, analyzing, and presenting data — there are already many 
established approaches in our field. But visualization has always been 
the area I find most interesting, because it is the most intuitive way 
to communicate findings.

I used to present clinical data through Shiny applications. Now I am 
exploring how to bring interactive visualization directly into a real 
web environment. This is still a work in progress, and today I am 
sharing an early draft — I feel there is a lot of potential here worth 
exploring further.

---

## What I Built

An interactive patient timeline using **R and D3.js**, integrating:

- Screening & Enrollment
- Medication records (First Dose / Last Dose)
- Adverse Events (with severity)
- Survival status

All in a single view — so reviewers can see a patient's complete 
journey at a glance.

![Patient Timeline Demo](../images/patient-timeline.png){style="border-radius: 10px;" width="800"}

---

## How It Works

The R side is simple: a data frame with event types, study days, 
and severity is passed directly into a D3.js script using the 
`r2d3` package. No CDISC-formatted datasets required — raw CRF 
data goes in, and the timeline comes out.

On the JavaScript side, `r2d3` automatically converts the R data 
frame into a row-oriented JSON array. Each event is plotted as a 
colored circle on a time axis, with labels alternating above and 
below to avoid overlap.

One key design choice: **study day zero is excluded from the axis**, 
since Day 0 has no clinical meaning in this context.

---

## Why This Matters

In clinical data review, reviewers often need to switch between 
multiple reports to piece together one patient's story. A timeline 
view solves this by putting everything in one place — clearly and 
interactively.

---

## What's Next

This is an early draft. The next steps include:

- Adding **tooltip** interactions
- Building a **population-level view** for cross-patient comparison
- Adding **filtering and zoom** functionality
